config.android.target.enum0: 64-bit ARM: every phone made since about 2015 - the fastest build and the smallest APK
config.android.target.enum2: x86-64: the Android emulator on a PC
config.android.target.enum4: Every architecture in one APK - four times the size and the build time
config.android.target.markdownDescriptio: Which Android architecture `GoForms: Build for Android` packages. One APK per build; pick `android` for all four.
config.androidNdkPath.markdownDescriptio: Path to the Android NDK root (the folder containing `source.properties` and `toolchains/`). Leave empty to search `ANDROID_NDK_HOME`, `ANDROID_HOME/ndk/*`, `~/Android/android-ndk-*`, `C:\\android-ndk-*` and the other usual places. `GoForms: Open Setup Guide` explains where to put a downloaded NDK.
config.build.offline.markdownDescription: Run builds with `GOPROXY=off`, so a module missing from the local cache fails immediately by name rather than waiting on a download. Builds never need the network as long as `go mod download` has run once; turn this on to have that verified rather than assumed.
config.frameworkPath.description: Absolute path to a local GoForms checkout (the folder containing go.mod for the goforms module). Used as the `replace goforms => ...` target when scaffolding new projects. Leave empty to be prompted the first time it's needed.
config.fynePath.markdownDescription: Full path to the `fyne` command-line tool (`go install fyne.io/tools/cmd/fyne@latest` puts it in `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`). Needed only for Android builds. Leave empty to search `PATH` and the Go bin directory.
config.goPath.markdownDescription: Full path to the `go` executable, for when the editor cannot find one itself. A GUI editor inherits the desktop session's `PATH`, not the one your `.bashrc`/`.zshrc` builds, so a Go installed under `/usr/local/go/bin` or managed by asdf/mise is often invisible to it even though it works in your terminal. Leave empty to search `goforms.goPath`, `go.goroot`, `GOROOT`, `PATH`, and the usual install locations, in that order.
